# aarambh-studio v2.0.0

aarambh-studio v2.0.0 is the second production source release of the ground-up
Rust LLM application. It completes Phases 16–28 and expands the v1 transformer,
training, inference, quantisation, safety, and self-learning stack with long
context, evaluation, multimodal training, distributed training, preference
alignment, accelerated decoding, structured tool calls, and local serving.

## Distribution Policy

- This is a GitHub source release of an application, not a crates.io library release.
- All 16 library crates and the CLI remain `publish = false`.
- GitHub's automatic source archives are the only release assets.
- No pretrained checkpoint, adapter, tokenizer, optimizer state, SafeTensors,
  GGUF file, or compiled CPU/CUDA binary is included.
- Users train, convert, fine-tune, quantise, and serve their own local checkpoints.

## v2 Highlights

### Long Context And Evaluation

- YaRN, NTK-aware, and linear RoPE scaling with backward-compatible unscaled behavior.
- Progressive 4K, 8K, and 16K context schedules without a quadratic persistent mask.
- Preallocated long-context KV caches for autoregressive decoding.
- `aarambh-studio eval` with perplexity, MMLU-lite, HellaSwag, GSM8K, HumanEval-lite,
  preference, image-caption, VQA, and tool-calling tasks.
- JSON and Markdown scorecards plus before/after comparison.

### Fine-Tuning And Alignment

- DoRA and QDoRA adapters with trainable weight magnitudes and low-rank directions.
- VLM DoRA/QDoRA instruction tuning with a frozen vision encoder and optional
  projector updates.
- DPO and QDPO preference tuning with stable pairwise loss, cached reference
  log-probabilities, reference-free ablation, and preference win-rate evaluation.
- Existing LoRA, QLoRA, SFT, tool SFT, GRPO, merge, and adapter formats remain available.

### Vision And Self-Learning

- Frozen CLIP-style ViT encoder, local image preprocessing, trainable projector,
  and LLaVA-style image-prefix fusion.
- Projector pretraining and VQA instruction data support.
- `infer --image` and multimodal evaluation.
- Vision-aware replay entries, projected-token caching, grounded color/counting/
  yes-no verifiers, and CUDA-gated multimodal self-learning.
- Text-only CPU self-learning remains available with deferred gradients and replay.

### Scale And Performance

- Optional top-k Mixture-of-Experts FFNs with load-balancing loss and utilization metrics.
- Single-node NCCL data-parallel training with deterministic sharded loaders,
  gradient averaging, rank-zero logging/checkpoints, and single-GPU fallback.
- Exact speculative decoding with Tiny draft models, block verification,
  rejection correction, KV rollback, telemetry, and greedy parity.
- Flash Attention v2 and fused CUDA kernels remain optional, with optimized AVX2,
  FMA, AVX-512, Rayon, and Candle fallback paths on CPU.

### Tool Use And Local Serving

- JSON Schema-constrained function calls that remain structurally valid during decoding.
- Typed tool definitions, tool choices, thinking integration, exact speculative
  composition, atomic structured output, tool SFT, and selection evaluation.
- Tool calls are emitted only; Aarambh does not execute commands, URLs, or APIs.
- Axum 0.8.9 OpenAI-compatible endpoints:
  - `POST /v1/chat/completions`
  - `POST /v1/completions`
  - `GET /v1/models`
  - `GET /healthz`
  - `GET /readyz`
  - `GET /metrics`
- JSON and SSE responses, continuous batching, chunked prefill, independent KV
  caches, bounded admission, disconnect cancellation, and graceful shutdown.
- Streaming safety scans rolling cross-token windows before release, redacts PII,
  terminates toxic output with `content_filter`, and keeps tool-call JSON atomic.

## Production Hardening

- Every package reports version `2.0.0`; `aarambh-studio --version` matches the tag.
- Rust 1.89 is the MSRV because the optimized AVX-512 path uses intrinsics stabilized there.
- `Cargo.lock` is committed and all CI/release commands use `--locked`.
- The release profile uses `opt-level=3`, Thin LTO, one codegen unit, and stripped debug info.
- Direct tokenizer dependencies align on the 0.22 line used by Candle.
- Every exported Rust API is documented and `missing_docs` is denied.
- Every unsafe block has an explicit safety rationale and Clippy enforces it.
- The release audit rejects unfinished implementation markers, unchecked roadmap
  tasks, publishable packages, version drift, and tracked model artifacts.
- CI validates stable Rust, Rust 1.89, formatting, checks, Clippy, tests, rustdoc,
  release build, CLI coverage, shell syntax, and RustSec advisories.

## Install From Source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/AarambhDevHub/aarambh-studio.git
cd aarambh-studio
git checkout v2.0.0
cargo build --release -p aarambh-studio --locked
target/release/aarambh-studio --version
```

For a local Cargo installation from the checked-out source:

```sh
cargo install --path aarambh-studio --locked
aarambh-studio --version
```

## Start The Local Server

```sh
aarambh-studio serve \
  --config configs/tiny_shakespeare.toml \
  --model checkpoints/tiny_shakespeare/step_000050/model.safetensors \
  --tokenizer checkpoints/tiny_shakespeare/tokenizer.json \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8080
```

The default loopback bind does not require authentication. Non-loopback binds
require a bearer token. The server lists and serves only checkpoints already
present on the host.

## Compatibility

- Existing dense model configurations remain valid when `rope_scaling` and `moe`
  are absent.
- Existing v1 text-only tokenizer IDs and checkpoint paths remain supported.
- Replay v1 entries load with no image reference.
- Existing LoRA/DoRA adapter merge and SafeTensors/GGUF inference paths remain available.
- v2.0.x is the supported release line; v1.0.x is no longer maintained.

## Known Boundaries

- No pretrained model quality claim is made because no weights are distributed.
- Vision self-learning, VLM tuning, MoE training, and distributed training require GPU hardware.
- Multi-GPU support is single-node NCCL; multi-node training is out of scope.
- MoE uses correctness-first dense masked dispatch rather than sparse grouped dispatch.
- Tool calls are single-call and emit-only; execution and multi-step agent loops are out of scope.
- The inference server is local/self-hosted and does not claim every OpenAI endpoint or parameter.
- CUDA throughput depends on the GPU, driver, toolkit, shape, and dtype; hardware timing is not a CI gate.

## Security

- Streaming and non-streaming requests pass through the configured safety policy.
- Non-loopback server binds require bearer authentication.
- Request bodies and queues are bounded, CORS is opt-in, and internal errors are sanitized.
- Safety audit logs store prompt hashes rather than raw prompts.
- Structured tool calls are validated and never executed by the inference engine.

See `CHANGELOG.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_V2.md`, `ROADMAP_V2.md`, and `RELEASE.md`
for the complete engineering history and release procedure.
